assertions_contracts.best_practice: Overview exposes ODIN_DISABLE_ASSERT tied to the -disable-assert switch and #assert for compile-time facts; core:testing provides expect_assert helpers. Nothing official contradicts the assert-for-invariants / return-for-input split.
assertions_contracts.evidence: Fresh re-read of the current guide confirms the position is unchanged and still accurate; pkg core:testing page fetched live this pass (generated with dev-2026-10, 2026-10-14) still lists expect_assert_from and expect_assert_message.
assertions_contracts.guide_position: Assertions enforce programmer-established invariants only; malformed external data returns a structured rejection; never put required state changes inside an assertion (guide section 6).

bounded_work.best_practice: No official bounded-work style guide exists. The FAQ (fetched live) documents bounds checking togglable per statement (#no_bounds_check / #bounds_check), and the Overview lists ODIN_NO_BOUNDS_CHECK and ODIN_DISABLE_ASSERT as explicit opt-out switches, so checks-on is the default posture the guide builds on. Stricter-than-default Tiger policy, not a contradiction.
bounded_work.evidence: FAQ and Overview re-fetched 2026-10-14 agree with the guide's model; no contradicting official position found.
bounded_work.guide_position: Bound all loops, queues, retries, memory, nesting and time with named limits; check sizes before allocation, indexing and multiplication; keep bounds checks in release (guide sections 5 and 7).

concurrency.best_practice: Official docs remain thin: core provides thread/sync primitives and dev-2026-10 extended core:sync/chan recv/try_recv to .Recv channels and multithreaded the semantic checker. No official concurrency style guide contradicts the guide; its discipline is project policy layered on primitives.
concurrency.evidence: dev-2026-10 release notes fetched live this pass confirm the chan change and the multithreaded checker; nothing in them revises any guide claim.
concurrency.guide_position: One owner or a documented synchronization protocol per mutable object, visible lock order, no broad lock across blocking/foreign calls, bounded queues, monotonic deadlines, generation tokens, ARM64-valid ordering arguments (guide section 11).

error_handling.best_practice: The FAQ (fetched live) rejects exceptions in favour of plain error handling through multiple return values, and the Overview documents the or_else, or_return, or_continue and or_break operators built on that idiom, with named results required for multi-value or_return.
error_handling.evidence: The guide's model still matches the official one. The naming gap from run 1 persists: a full-text search of the current guide and SKILL.md this pass finds zero occurrences of or_return / or_else / or_continue / or_break, so the idiomatic propagation spelling is still unnamed (carried as a proposal).
error_handling.guide_position: Use a result enum or (value, error) consistently, no plausible default after failure, preserve commit-point distinctions; validate external input with ordinary control flow (guide section 10).

formatting.guide_position: Baseline table: four-space house style, 100-column target, odinfmt (from ols) configured by a reviewed odinfmt.json, with the house values explicitly differing from the ols example defaults; section 19 names ols/odinfmt, states the compiler has no fmt subcommand, and requires the house values to be written into odinfmt.json.

memory_ownership.best_practice: core:mem states ownership in Odin is not strict unlike Rust, new/free and make/delete default to context.allocator, and documents the Arena, Dynamic_Arena, Scratch, Rollback_Stack and Tracking_Allocator families. That matches the guide's model.
memory_ownership.evidence: dev-2026-10 release notes fetched live this pass again list the core:mem revert of a change that misunderstood mem.Scratch semantics plus new Scratch tests, reinforcing the guide's warning. The run-1 dated-caution proposal is still unapplied: the guide contains no Scratch-semantics caution (full-text search this pass finds Scratch only in a reset checklist line), so the proposal is carried forward.
memory_ownership.guide_position: Explicit allocator, owner, lifetime and failure path for every allocation; context.allocator is ambient and must be captured across threads/callbacks; arenas are not automatically bounded; a tracking allocator exposes leaks but proves nothing (guide sections 8 and 9).

security.best_practice: No official Odin secure-coding guide exists. The language ships core:crypto packages (dev-2026-10 touches core:crypto/aegis docs and a P-256 fiat fix) and sanitizer flags, but application security remains a library/project responsibility, exactly as the guide assumes. Stricter Tiger policy, not contradicted.
security.evidence: dev-2026-10 notes and Overview sanitizer constants re-fetched 2026-10-14; absence of an official security style doc is reported rather than filled by inference.
security.guide_position: Authenticate and authorize workers, validate framed messages before allocation, use established TLS/crypto with verification, keep secrets out of argv/logs/crash artifacts, parameterized DB work, bounded pools and results, narrow OS privileges (guide section 13).

static_analysis.best_practice: The compiler and OLS expose concrete check surfaces: checker_args such as -strict-style passed through ols (the OLS README Neovim example uses exactly that), per-file #+vet controls in the Overview, and -sanitize with Address, Memory and Thread flags surfaced as ODIN_SANITIZER_FLAGS.
static_analysis.evidence: Still unapplied from run 1: a full-text search of the current guide this pass finds no -vet, -strict-style, -warnings-as-errors or -sanitize flag set; section 19 still says only that compiler checking, formatter checking, tests and sanitizer support are separate gates. OLS README and the Overview vet/sanitizer entries were verified live this pass.
static_analysis.guide_position: Compile with diagnostics at full strength, keep assertions and bounds checks, treat formatter/compiler/test/sanitizer as separate gates (guide section 19); no concrete flag set is named anywhere in the guide or SKILL.md.

(including an -o:speed variant), covering boundaries, allocator exhaustion, failure-before-commit, races and stale handles; the reference package is explicitly marked not compiled here (guide sections 18 and 19).
